articles.title: Zambian NWSL players must wait to return from international duty
articles.summary: Three Zambian players for National Women's Soccer League teams are not yet able to return to the United State following an international match because of U....
articles.body:
Three Zambian players for National Women's Soccer League teams are not yet able to return to the United State following an international match because of U.S. travel protocols surrounding the Ebola outbreak.

Barbra Banda of the Orlando Pride, Racheal Kundananji of the Chicago Stars and Prisca Chilufya of Angel City took part in an Oct. 8 match in Uganda.

"Following their participation with the Zambian Women's National Team during the recent international window, several players are currently observing U.S. government public health re-entry protocols required for travelers returning from the East African region," the NWSL said in a statement Friday. "The NWSL is working with its clubs and U.S. immigration to ensure the players' safe return; all players are in excellent health.

Zambia played a two-legged series with Uganda as part of qualification for the 2028 Los Angele Olympics earlier this month. The first match was in Uganda, where there were 20 confirmed cases of Ebola this summer.

Zambia fell 2-1 loss to Uganda in the first match in Kampala, but won the second leg 4-1 that advanced Zambia 5-3 on aggregate.

The absence of those players comes at a crucial time in the NWSL season, with only two regular-season games left before the playoffs.

The United States has imposed a 21-day waiting or quarantine period for re-entry on travelers who have been in the Congo, Uganda and South Sudan due to to the Ebola outbreak.

The current Ebola outbreak was declared in mid-May after spreading in a remote part of eastern Congo. The nation's Health Ministry recently reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths .

Last week, Kenya became the second country after Uganda to report an Ebola case imported from Congo .

articles.title: Alabama football offensive line starter ruled out for Tennessee

articles.body:
Alabama football will officially be without its starting center against Tennessee .

Racin Delgatty (lower body) was ruled out according to Alabama 's third SEC availability report heading into Saturday's game against Tennessee. Delgatty joins defensive linemen Jeremiah Beaman and Terrance Green, linebackers Desmond Umeozulu and Cayden Jones, defensive back Nick Sherman and wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams as Crimson Tide players out against the Volunteers due to injury.

Alabama linebacker Justin Hill remains probable. Alabama tight end Josh Ford was added to the injury list Friday and is questionable.

Delgatty was questionable in Alabama's initial availability report before he was downgraded to doubtful Thursday.

Mal Waldrep Jr. is expected to be Alabama's center with Delgatty out. Waldrep has taken 150 snaps at left guard across four games in 2026, per Pro Football Focus. He's accounted for three pressures and one sack.

"Mal takes a ton of reps there," Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb said. "Does a really good job, smart, tough, dependable. He'll do a good job."

Alabama kicks off against Tennessee at 2:30 p.m. CT Saturday, Oct. 17, at Neyland Stadium. The game will air on ABC.

articles.title: Zambia women's national team players to miss NWSL games while undergoing Ebola travel restriction protocols
articles.summary: 3 NWSL players, including top forward Barbra Banda, joined the Copper Queens for a friendly in Uganda, but will now be out until the end of the month due to...
articles.body:
Three members of the Zambian women's national team will miss multiple NWSL games while following a multi-week Centers for Disease Control (CDC) protocol due to Ebola travel restrictions, the league announced Friday.

In a statement shared with multiple outlets, the NWSL said that the players are all "in excellent health," though they did not name any of the specific players affected.

"Following their participation with the Zambian Women's National Team during the recent international window, several players are currently observing U.S. government public health re-entry protocols required for travelers returning from the East African region," the league said in the statement. "The NWSL is working with its clubs and U.S. immigration to ensure the players' safe return; all players are in excellent health."

The Copper Queens played two matches against Uganda over the past week as part of CAF qualification for the 2028 Olympics, playing the team in Uganda on Oct. 8 before playing in Zambia on Oct. 13. The Zambian team lost the first game 2-1, before earning a decisive 4-1 win at home.

Current CDC guidelines indicate that non-U.S. citizens traveling from Uganda (along with the Democratic Republic of Congo and South Sudan) must wait 21 days before returning to the United States due to concerns about an Ebola outbreak.

The 21-day period, which presumably dates back to when they left Uganda after the first match, will seemingly expire toward the end of October. The final games of the NWSL regular season will all take place on Nov. 1 in a Decision Day format, with all games kicking off at 5 p.m. ET.

Three NWSL players, all forwards, were called up to the Zambian team during this window: Orlando Pride's Barbra Banda, Angel City FC's Prisca Chilufya and Chicago Stars' Racheal Kundananji.

With the current timeline, Banda, Chilufya and Kundananji seem likely to miss a minimum of two games, if not all three games left in the regular season.

Banda has been one of the top scorers in the league over the past few years, currently sitting second on the league's scoring list with 17 goals. Kundananji was just acquired by Chicago last week after three seasons with Bay FC.

Only Chilufya is on a team that is still in the playoff race: Angel City is currently in sixth place in the league and striving to stay in the top eight in order to advance to the postseason. The Stars are dead last in the league and have been out of the playoffs for weeks; the Pride are in 11th place, and are functionally eliminated from the postseason.

articles.title: Ohio State vs. Indiana predictions from our Buckeyes Wire writers
articles.summary: Ohio State travels to Indiana to take on a top five ranked Hoosier club. Our Buckeyes Wire staff make their predictions for the game.
articles.body:
There's a game that's been circled on the Big Ten calendar since the offseason, and it's almost here. The Indiana Hoosiers took down the Ohio State Buckeyes in the Big Ten Championship game last year in a classic, then went on to win the College Football Playoff national championship.

Now, it's time for the rematch, and it takes place in Bloomington, where the Buckeyes will have to try to get things done in hostile territory. The winner will be the favorite to win the Big Ten, while the loser will have some work to do. It should be a close one, and Vegas agrees, with Ohio State listed as a very modest favorite .

Before each Ohio State football game, we like to ask our writers to go out on a limb and predict the outcome of the game, and with such a huge one on the doorstep, opinions vary on this one.

Here is what our writers at Buckeyes Wire predict will happen between Ohio State and Indiana on Saturday.

Ohio State vs. Indiana, according to Phil Harrison, Lead Writer/Editor

One game can be an exception, but two is a pattern. This isn't the same Indiana team we saw last year. We watched the Hoosiers struggle against Northwestern and Nebraska , the only teams with a pulse Curt Cignetti's crew has played. The offense hasn't been as dynamic, and the defense isn't creating the negative plays at the rate it did last season. The Buckeyes will not run all over Indiana on the ground, but they will have plenty of success through the air, just enough to pull out a huge victory.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 27, Indiana 24

Ohio State vs. Indiana, according to Mark Russell, Featured Writer

Ohio State gets a shot at redemption when it goes to Indiana for a rematch of the Big Ten Championship from a year ago. But these are two different teams. The Buckeyes are facing some injury issues, the most concerning of which is offensive lineman Austin Sierveld. Ohio State has struggled a bit to protect quarterback Julian Sayin, while the Hoosiers' pass rush is the best in the Big Ten. But if the line can keep Sayin clean, he should have time to carve up a suspect Indiana secondary. It'll be a tough environment, but the Buckeyes get a score late to seal the victory.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 27, Indiana 17

Ohio State vs. Indiana, according to Alec Lasley, Featured Writer

I fully anticipate OSU will try to get out of the gates hot, something Indiana has dealt with on its own at times this season: slow starts. If Ohio State can't get going early, it's going to put a lot of pressure on the Sayin-Smith connection, and that's when IU's defense will excel. It's going to be a close one, but I think Indiana playing at home and having the come-from-behind experience of last week under its belt will be a huge positive variable. Hoosiers start strong, finish stronger, and limit some of the explosive plays the Buckeyes typically get.

Score Prediction: Indiana 24, Ohio State 17

articles.title: Dylan Raiola Benched Despite Dante Moore Injury in New Rumors Ahead of Oregon vs. UCLA
articles.summary: Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola is reportedly at risk of losing his spot as Dante Moore's injury replacement.
articles.body:
Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola is reportedly at risk of losing his spot as Dante Moore's injury replacement.

CBS Sports' Chris Hummer and Matt Zenitz reported Friday the Ducks are "trending toward" starting third-stringer Brock Thomas over Raiola against Nebraska this Saturday.

Biggest Disappointments of 2026 CFB Season 😞

Updated College Football Playoff Predictions

Moore has been ruled out for Sunday after suffering a head injury in a Week 4 matchup against USC.

After a Week 5 bye, Raiola made a Week 6 start in Moore's absence but was benched for Thomas in the fourth quarter of last Saturday's loss to UCLA.

Raiola and Thomas were taking reps at practice this week alongside Akili Smith Jr., according to On3's Pete Nakos . Ducks head coach Dan Lanning told reporters earlier this week Smith was "absolutely" factoring into the quarterback competition.

When asked if Wednesday if he was considering playing multiple quarterbacks against Nebraska, Lanning said, "I believe in doing whatever it takes to win... all things are on the table."

Raiola went 6-for-19 with 43 passing yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions through three quarters last Saturday.

That marked a disappointing follow-up to his performance in relief of Moore in Week 5, during which he went 19-for-25 with two touchdowns and no picks to close out a win at USC.

"I think last week we were able to get to our first decision quite a bit. There were some times that [Raiola] was able to evade the pass rush and create successful plays," Lanning said after the loss to UCLA. "We weren't able to create that today."

Thomas came in to start the fourth against UCLA. He fumbled on his first drive of the game and settled for a field goal on his next possession before wideout Evan Stewart turned a short pass into a 44-yard touchdown to get the Ducks within two points of tying the game.

The Ducks got halfway down the field on the game's final drive before conceding the 17-15 loss. Thomas finished the fourth quarter having gone 11-for-15 with 156 yards and one touchdown.

Lanning said shortly after the loss it would be "worth evaluating" whether Thomas should be moved above Raiola in the depth chart.

Thomas committed to Oregon as a three-star prospect in 2023 and appeared in seven games for the Ducks as a redshirt sophomore last season. Smith is a former four-star recruit who did not appear in a game as a true freshman last season.

Raiola, who holds a projected On3 NIL valuation of $500,000, started for two seasons at Nebraska before transferring to Oregon to back up Moore this offseason. He will now wait to see if he gets any playing time against his former Cornhuskers teammates when Saturday's game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET in Eugene.

articles.title: Su señoría se puso las botas: de jugar con Osasuna al crimen de Yesa
articles.standfirst: Después de estrenarse con el primer equipo rojillo a los 18 años, pero de abandonar el fútbol a los 23 por las lesiones, Javier Martínez Tabernero se ha convertido en juez titular
articles.summary: Después de estrenarse con el primer equipo rojillo a los 18 años, pero de abandonar el fútbol a los 23 por las lesiones, Javier Martínez Tabernero se ha convertido en juez titular
articles.body: La cita con MARCA se retrasa, porque ha llegado un caso de violencia de genero. “Para eso estamos siempre de guardia”, asegura su señoría. Ejea de los Caballeros (Zaragoza) tiene dos juzgados de primera instancia e instrucción en la misma dirección. El titular de uno de ellos es Javier Alfonso Martínez Tabernero, que, entonces tenía 28 años, ocupó la plaza en febrero. Hacía poco más de un lustro que se había retirado del fútbol, en el que, entre otras, defendió la camiseta del primer equipo de Osasuna. “Parece una trayectoria corta, pero a mí se me ha hecho larga. Son como dos vidas diferentes, un cambio brutal. Pasas de entrenar tres horas al día a meterte en tu habitación 14 para estudiar las oposiciones”, explica una vez finalizado el juicio en audiencia pública. “Yo empiezo la carrera de Derecho a los 18 años, compaginándola con el fútbol y casi por inercia, porque me coincidían mejor los horarios que por ejemplo en una Ingeniería Mecánica, que era mi primera idea. Pero me empieza a gustar y en las prácticas de tercero ya veo que encaja en mi manera de ser y en lo que puedo aportar”. Javier vivía y vive en Huesca, pero toda su familia es de Pamplona y de hecho nació allí. No resulta extraño, así, que a los 14 años, después de formarse en la Escuela de Fútbol Oscense y en el Peñas Oscenses, recibiera con especial ilusión, entre todas las que tenía, la oferta de Osasuna. Los dos primeros años se desplazaba para entrenamientos y partidos, “tenía la sensación de que vivía en el coche”, hasta que por fin pudo afincarse. Todo iba bien, o todo parecía ir bien. Y el 17 de octubre de 2015, mayor de edad apenas por unos meses, futbolista del Promesas aún, se estrenó como futbolista del primer equipo en el tramo final de un partido contra el Albacete. Para tomar la alternativa, no pudo tener mejor padrino. Porque entró en el campo sustituyendo a una leyenda como Nino, 35 años por aquel entonces. “La verdad es que hasta que no estás dentro y compartes el vestuario con este tipo de gente no te das cuenta del nivel al que se juega. Todo lo hacía bien... y eso igual desde fuera no se ve”. Una semana después, Javier viajó a Tenerife pero no tuvo minutos. Dos semanas después, fue titular ante el Girona. “En el momento igual no lo valoras, pero ahora ya con el tiempo, aunque quede un poquito más borroso, lo recuerdas con cariño y sobre todo con orgullo. Al final debutar en Segunda con 18 años es una recompensa a un trabajo bien hecho, con todos los obstáculos que han ido saliendo y que has procurado sortear”. Aquel partido contra la escuadra gironí marcó un antes y un después: “Las lesiones me han lastrado siempre. Yo me acuerdo de que la primera vez que me lesioné tenía unos 12 años, igual menos, y mi entrenador ya andaba loco. O sea, es algo contra lo que he luchado toda mi vida... sin éxito. Pero después de aquel encuentro me empiezo a dar cuenta de que mi cuerpo no me sigue. Lo aguanto haciendo un esfuerzo físico muy alto, porque al final es Segunda, pero después me pego una semana en la que no puedo cambiar de ritmo, y a la siguiente sigo igual, mientras veo que otros compañeros van como aviones”. Martínez terminó saliendo de Osasuna para pasar por el Cerceda, por el Izarra y por el Real Unión... “Un club histórico en el que se portaron como señores conmigo y en el que la verdad empecé bien, pero ahí lo de las lesiones ya fue exacerbado, de no conseguir muchas veces ni completar tres entrenamientos. Llegó un momento en que decidí dejarlo. Me querían renovar, pero les dije que no podía más. Que mi salud mental no aguantaba. Y lo respetaron”. ¿Y por qué tanta lesión? “Me han propuesto muchas explicaciones... pero la realidad es que yo seguía lesionándome. Tengo una pierna más corta que otra, pero tampoco parece suficiente. Lo probé todo: fisioterapia, rehabilitaciones, tratamientos, cambio de plantillas... en Osasuna me desviaron a un fisio muy bueno, Jurdan Mendigutxia, que además es experto en isquios y que me permitió cierta regularidad, pero mi cuerpo no daba para competir”. Javier jugó el último partido en diciembre de 2020. Tenía 23 años. En enero de 2021 se encerró en su habitación. “Si soy sincero, cuando dejo el fútbol era tal el hastío, era tal la frustración, que empezar a estudiar y a llevar una vida sedentaria me parecía hasta bien. Me sentaba y pensaba: ‘Aquí no me voy a lesionar’”. Curiosamente, adelgazó: “Paso de entrenar tres horas al día, más luego gimnasio por la tarde, a de repente nada. Estudiaba seis días a la semana, librando uno, y esos seis eran de muchas horas. Así que apenas me daba un paseo... o ni eso. Además comía para marcar los tiempos de estudio, pero no porque tuviera hambre, y luego está toda la tensión de la oposición... Me convertí en un palo. Pasé de 78 o 79 kilos a unos 66 o 67 el día que aprobé“. Ese día tardó casi tres años en llegar, noviembre de 2023, en todo caso mucho menos de lo que suele tardar en ese tipo de oposiciones. Javier iba a ser juez: “Sin el fútbol tengo muy claro que yo no hubiera aprobado. Esa capacidad de tolerar la frustración, esa resiliencia... sobre todo aceptar que tú haces tu trabajo y que luego muchas cosas no dependen de ti. Se ha implementado como forma de pensar eso de ‘si quieres, puedes’. Pero no, si quieres a veces no puedes. En cualquier caso tú tienes que hacer tu trabajo e intentarlo con todo”. A partir de ahí, un año de formación en la Escuela Judicial de Barcelona, seis meses de prácticas (“estás con un magistrado que ya ha tomado posesión, pero aún no puedes firmar sentencias”), seis meses de destino provisional (”todavía no estás dentro de la carrera, pero ya puedes firmarlas”)... y por fin la oferta de plazas y la elección por orden de nota. En su caso sólo salió una para Aragón, la de Ejea, y tuvo la suerte de elegirla por delante de muchos otros. En febrero de 2026, Javier Martínez se convertía en juez titular. “Es bonito empezar aquí, porque al final el trato resulta mucho más cercano. Es un juzgado de pueblo, en el que estamos dos jueces y tienes competencias de todo. De instrucción, de violencia de género, de familia, de civil... y entonces ves muchas cosas. Hay gente para la que el conflicto jurídico es casi lo de menos, lo que necesita es contar su historia y que alguien la escuche. Eso este juzgado te lo permite. Al final la Justicia tiene unos medios deficientes, tanto personales como materiales, y hay una sensación y una situación un poco de atasco”. Uno de los primeros casos que lo esperaba tenía lo suyo. La aparición de restos humanos en el embalse de Yesa correspondía en principio al partido judicial de Ejea: “En un primer momento la verdad es que da respeto. Tú has estudiado y te has preparado, pero te surgen dudas. Desde la perspectiva profesional era un reto y lo afronté con entusiasmo. Y con mucho trabajo. Lo asumes como parte de tu oficio. Tienes 28 o 29 años, pero eres juez y debes tomar decisiones”. Terminó inhibiéndose, pero para entonces ya se había investigado y ya se había decretado prisión provisional sin fianza: “Al principio teníamos sólo el cuerpo del delito, pero no sabíamos dónde se había perpetrado el homicidio. Entonces la norma dice que el juez competente será el del partido judicial donde se hayan encontrado vestigios del delito. Luego ya avanzamos en la investigación y se revelaron indicios sólidos de que se había perpetrado en Pamplona. Entonces el fuero preferente es el del lugar en el que se comete el delito”. A Javier, por lo demás, le preocupan las acusaciones de politización de la Justicia: "Igual es meterme en camisa de once varas, pero se está realizando un ataque ya continuo hacia las decisiones judiciales, por parte de determinados sectores políticos, y lo considero muy grave. El juez en una torre de marfil, viendo las cosas desde arriba, es una figura que tampoco vale ya, pero lo importante de las sentencias es que estén motivadas y fundadas en derecho. No se resuelve bien o mal, sino fundado en derecho". - "¿Y en el fútbol? ¿Falta justicia en el fútbol?" - "Si nos metemos en lo que es el campo durante 90 minutos, yo creo que no. El fútbol es bastante duro y bastante justo en general. El verde no miente". Javier, que estuvo más de cuatro años sin tocar una pelota, se ha reenganchado en el Almudévar, de Tercera RFEF. “Empecé bien la temporada... pero ya me he roto el isquio”.

articles.title: El dato que amenaza al Betis: 3,2 goles por partido
articles.standfirst: Desde la llegada de Flick, han anotado 16 dianas a los andaluces
articles.summary: Desde la llegada de Flick, han anotado 16 dianas a los andaluces
articles.body: Si hay algo que caracteriza al Barcelona esta temporada, es su facilidad para ver portería. Y a este dato se suma que, desde la llegada de Hansi Flick al banquillo azulgrana en 2024, el Betis se ha convertido en una de sus víctimas predilectas. Los culés afrontan el encuentro de esta tarde con 34 goles a favor en LaLiga, una cifra que refleja su enorme potencial ofensivo y su capacidad para castigar a los rivales. Arroja una media de más de 4 dianas por compromiso. El conjunto verdiblanco conoce bien esa pegada. En los cinco enfrentamientos disputados contra el equipo de Flick, entre LaLiga y la Copa del Rey, el Barcelona ha marcado 16 goles, a una media de 3,2 tantos por partido. Un registro que evidencia las dificultades que ha tenido el Betis para contener el ataque azulgrana desde la llegada del técnico alemán. Durante la primera temporada de Flick al frente del Barcelona, ambos equipos se enfrentaron en tres ocasiones. El primer duelo, disputado en diciembre de 2024 en el campeonato liguero, terminó con empate a dos en feudo andaluz. Poco más de un mes después, en enero de 2025, los azulgranas se impusieron por un contundente 5-1 en los octavos de final de la Copa del Rey. Ya en la segunda vuelta de LaLiga, en abril, ambos conjuntos volvieron a firmar tablas, con un 1-1. La temporada siguiente mantuvo la misma tendencia ofensiva. El Barcelona se impuso al Betis en los dos enfrentamientos ligueros de 2025-26: primero, con un espectacular 5-3 en Sevilla en diciembre, y posteriormente, con un triunfo por 3-1 en mayo de este año. Ocho goles en dos partidos que confirmaron las dificultades del conjunto andaluz para frenar el caudal ofensivo de los catalanes. Más allá de los goles, hay otro dato que respalda el dominio azulgrana: Hansi Flick nunca ha perdido contra el Betis. El balance de estos cinco encuentros oficiales es de tres victorias y dos empates, sin ninguna derrota. Un precedente favorable que el Barcelona buscará prolongar en su próximo compromiso esta tarde contra el conjunto verdiblanco. De hecho, la última victoria de los andaluces contra el conjunto culé data de diciembre de 2021 en el Spotify Camp Nou con Xavi en el banquillo. Los locales cayeron por 0-1 con gol de Juanmi.

articles.title: Y ‘faltan’ Julián y Sorloth
articles.standfirst: Los máximos goleadores la temporada pasada, 40 tantos, todavía no se han estrenado. Ya han marcado 11 jugadores rojiblancos esta temporada.
articles.summary: Los máximos goleadores la temporada pasada, 40 tantos, todavía no se han estrenado. Ya han marcado 11 jugadores rojiblancos esta temporada.
articles.body: Baena, con cuatro goles, Jonathan David, con tres, y Grimaldo, con otros tres, completan el podio de los goleadores rojiblancos de la temporada. Hasta 11 jugadores (completan el listado Kang in, Barrios, Lookman, Llorente, Pubill, Giuliano, Cuti y Le Normand) del Atlético han participado en los tantos de un equipo que, con 10 jornadas disputadas, alcanza los 21 goles: 18 en LaLiga y 3 en la Champions. Numeros que superan los dos tantos por encuentro… pero que tienen un matiz especial. Y es que los dos máximos goleadores del Atlético en las dos últimas temporadas todavía no se han estrenado. Ni Julián, que firmó 29 y 20 tantos respectivamente, ni Sorloth, que logró 24 y 20, han sido capaces de celebrar una diana. Algo que en el caso del noruego es normal porque apenas ha disputado los últimos 17 minutos de Mendizorroza. Casi 100 goles (93, exactamente) entre los dos principales delanteros rojiblancos, que si el curso pasado tenían a Griezmann para completar la terna este tienen a Jonathan David como competencia como demuestran los tres tantos firmados por el canadiense en sus primeros 300 minutos de juego. Así, el del Espanyol será la primera bala en las próximas semanas para que ambos estrenen su casillero. Stuttgart, Deportivo y Levante son los siguientes antes de afrontar la que será la semana más importante, y difícil, de las que le quedan a los de Simeone en este 2026: la última antes del parón. Así, la primera semana de noviembre está marcada en rojo por la entidad de los rivales que pasarán por el Metropolitano. El 3 lo hará el Bayern en la cuarta jornada de Champions. El 9 un Barça de momento intratable que se le da especialmente bien a los dos delanteros que espera Simeone para completar su arsenal ofensivo: Julián y Sorloth.

articles.title: Mourinho y el Sevilla: un enfado colosal con el árbitro Taylor y la lista de los 13 errores
articles.standfirst: A causa de la final de la UEFA que perdió con la Roma ante los hispalenses en Budapest y de un partido dirigido por Clos Gómez en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: A causa de la final de la UEFA que perdió con la Roma ante los hispalenses en Budapest y de un partido dirigido por Clos Gómez en el Bernabéu
articles.body: La visita del Sevilla al Santiago Bernabéu se presenta cargada de electricidad... arbitral. La tensión se ha disparado entre el Real Madrid, el colectivo arbitral y la Federación. La ausencia de rueda de prensa tras el partido ante el Villarreal y las posteriores declaraciones de Mourinho después del duelo con la Roma dibujan una noche de dinamita en el Bernabéu. El Sevilla es un capítulo especial de la larga colección de choques y desencuentros de Mourinho con los árbitros. En este caso, el marco está en las competiciones europeas. Después de ganar la Conference en 2022, la Roma fue finalista de la Europa League en la temporada siguiente. Para aquella final, ante el Sevilla, en Budapest, la UEFA designó al inglés Anthony Taylor. El título acabó en Nervión, por séptima vez, después de un partido de alto voltaje, resuelto en los penaltis y en enfado hisórico de Mourinho con el árbitro. "¡Eres una puta vergüenza, eres una puta vergüenza!", le gritó Mourinho al acabar la final. Eso le valió una apertura de expediente por parte de la UEFA y cuatro partidos de sanción. La rabia del entrenador portugués la expuso en la rueda de prensa. Después de un primer mensaje de queja que parecía no ir a más, explotó: "Nos vamos a casa muertos por una injusticia. Pero fue un gran partido, una gran final. El árbitro parecía español, tantas tarjetas amarillas. Y luego cuando le tenía que sacar la segunda a Lamela, él no la sacó. Y luego marcó uno de los penaltis. Es una injusticia". Fue en el parking del Puskas Arena donde Mourinho, teléfono en mano, mostró una jugada: el penalti pitado a favor del Sevilla en el que tuvo que intervenir el VAR para anularlo. Ante la ira del portugués, Roberto Rosetti, responsable arbitral de la UEFA, trató de abrazar y calmar a Mourinho. De nada valió. "Estuviste de acuerdo con ellos", fue la respuesta. Dirigiéndose de nuevo al árbitro inglés, añadió, en referencia al penalti inicialmente concedido y luego anulado a favor del Sevilla: "Hasta Rosetti dijo que no era penalti, y tú no fuiste capaz de verlo" Meses después, cuando se le recordó lo vivido en la capital húngaro, Mourinho dejó claro que no olvidada: "No digo lo que pienso de Taylor porque me sancionan con diez partidos". En diciembre de 2010, en su primera temporada en Madrid, la visita del Sevilla acabó en un 1-0 con gol de Di María. Y con Mourinho en la sala de prensa con una lista de 13 errores del árbitro. Era Clos Gómez, después, desde marzo de 2018, primer responsable del VAR en España. Esta era la lista: 1.- Minuto 9. Falta de Konko a Di María que debe ser amarilla y no la muestra. 2.- minuto 14. Fuera de juego de Özil que no era. 3.- minuto 20. Fuera de juego de Benzema que no era. 4. minuto 24. Falta de Zokora a Khedira en la que no saca amarilla. 5.- minuto 25. Falta a Cristiano en la frontal que no pita. 6.- minuto 34. Fuera de juego del Sevilla que no pita. 7.- minuto 39. Falta a Ozil que no pita. 8.- minuto 43. Fuera de juego de Di María que pita y no era. 9.- En el descanso añade 1 minuto cuando era más. 10.- minuto 47. Fuera de Juego de Ozil que no era. 11.- minuto 64. Segunda amarilla a Carvalho por darse un cabezazo con Negredo en un salto. 12.- minuto 69. Penalti de Escudé a Granero que no pita. 13.- minuto 78’. Tarjeta a Özil en el cambio por perder tiempo, las pérdidas del Sevilla no son castigadas igual. Mou fue más allá. Pidió que el club se sumara a su denuncia. Reclamó una reunión inmediata con Florentino Pérez al sentirse cansado de ser él quien se lleva las sanciones por dar la cara representando a la entidad. "Me dan una lista con trece errores graves. Me preguntaron si me cansaba la presión. No, porque no me siento presionado al hacer las cosas que me gustan: entrenar y jugar. De lo que estoy un poco cansado es de que me den una lista de errores graves del árbitro y quieran que sea yo quien ataque al árbitro y defienda a mi equipo. Tiene que ser defendido porque lo merece hoy y muchas veces más. Si yo cojo esto y voy para adelante, la historia es siempre la misma: suspensión para Mourinho. Tenemos un club, un organigrama, y quiero que la gente defienda a mi equipo, no solo yo. Lo que ha pasado hoy no merece ni comentario", en un mensaje que apuntaba a una crítica al club y, sin nombrarlas, a las figuras del director general deportivo, Jorge Valdano, y de Miguel Pardeza, director deportivo. Era un paso al frente de Mourinho. Como el que dio en Roma. Pero ahora sabe que él es la principal voz del Madrid.

articles.title: Otro cambio en el Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El Madrid volverá a sustituir el césped tras el partido de la NFL, pese a que el actual está en perfectas condiciones
articles.summary: El Madrid volverá a sustituir el césped tras el partido de la NFL, pese a que el actual está en perfectas condiciones
articles.body: Otra vez, la misma operación. El Real Madrid volverá a cambiar el césped del Santiago Bernabéu después del partido de la NFL. Una renovación que, esta vez, no responde a los problemas que durante años convirtieron el terreno de juego en uno de los grandes quebraderos de cabeza del club. Todo lo contrario: en Valdebebas están encantados con su estado actual y consideran que, por fin, han dado con la tecla para acabar con el calvario del césped. Sin embargo, el paso de la NFL por el estadio obligará a empezar de nuevo. El calendario ya marca la hoja de ruta. El Madrid disputará su último partido en casa antes del evento frente al Valencia. Al día siguiente, el 8 de noviembre, el Bernabéu acogerá el enfrentamiento entre los Atlanta Falcons y los Cincinnati Bengals. El fútbol americano dejará su huella sobre el terreno de juego y el club tendrá que acometer una nueva sustitución para devolverlo a las condiciones necesarias para la competición. El peso de los jugadores, los apoyos, los cambios de dirección y el contacto constante con la superficie hacen difícil que el césped soporte el evento sin sufrir daños importantes. "Después de que deportistas de más de 100 kilos se peguen por el césped, lo normal es que quede en muy malas condiciones", advertían desde el club el año pasado. La intervención estará planificada al milímetro para reducir al máximo el tiempo de recuperación. Una vez celebrado el partido, el objetivo será retirar el terreno afectado y colocar el nuevo césped para que el Bernabéu vuelva a estar preparado para el fútbol. El parón de selecciones posterior ofrece una ventana de trabajo especialmente útil para avanzar en la operación sin la presión inmediata de un partido de Liga en casa. La intención es que el nuevo tapete esté listo para el encuentro frente al Celta, previsto para el 22 de noviembre, que coincidirá con el regreso de Vinicius tras cumplir su sanción de 4 partidos. Desde el Real Madrid se han mostrado muy críticos con el horario del encuentro en Mestalla, al considerar que el equipo tendrá que afrontar una cita exigente con apenas 72 horas de margen después de jugar en Atenas su partido de Champions. "Los horarios son la gran arma de Tebas y los utiliza una y otra vez para ir contra el Real Madrid", aseguran desde RMTV. La queja del club contrasta la opinión de los jugadores del Madrid, que están encantados con la fecha elegida para dicho partido. El encuentro ante el Valencia se disputará el sábado 7 de noviembre, lo que les permitirá tener el domingo libre para acudir al Bernabéu y disfrutar en directo del partido de la NFL entre los Atlanta Falcons y los Cincinnati Bengals. Si el compromiso liguero se hubiera fijado para el domingo 8, como así deseaba el club blanco, la plantilla no podría haber asistido al partido. Y es que en el vestuario del Real Madrid hay más de un apasionado de la NFL. Por eso, más allá del enfado del club con los horarios de LaLiga, la plantilla tiene motivos para celebrar la fecha final.

articles.title: Los minutos de furia del Madrid: "No queremos rendirnos"
articles.standfirst: La virtud oculta que ha dado alas al equipo en los momentos de dificultad
articles.summary: La virtud oculta que ha dado alas al equipo en los momentos de dificultad
articles.body: El Madrid es un equipo con problemas en el juego, pero vivo. Más allá del sufrimiento al que le lleva su atasco futbolístico para ganar los partidos, el equipo ha demostrado una rebeldía que lo ha sacado de más de un apuro. Roma no sólo fue el último ejemplo, también el reconocimiento a una virtud oculta entre las dificultades para ganar de forma más holgada. "Con rebeldía empezamos a hacer lo que trabajamos. Estoy orgulloso de que el equipo tenga rebeldía", dijo Valverde tras la remontada en el Olímpico. Algo que también destacó Mourinho: "Remontamos por el coraje de los jugadores". Porque lo de Roma no fue un milagro, fue un ejercicio de orgullo. Y no es la primera vez que lo demuestra el Real Madrid en lo que va de temporada. Hasta en seis ocasiones lo ha sacado a relucir con el partido cuesta arriba. No siempre ha logrado el objetivo en el arreón final, pero sí ha dejado una imagen de inconformismo en lo que el equipo da con la tecla para jugar mejor y no abusar del orgullo y coraje. El Madrid ha jugado 10 partidos y en seis de ellos ha protagonizado minutos de furia en la recta final. Lo hizo ante el Espanyol, logrando un valioso triunfo en el 90'. Mismo guion que ante el Elche. También en las derrotas frente a Betis y Atlético. En La Cartuja llegó a disponer de un penalti que falló Mbappé para empatar y en el Metropolitano, estando con 10, no le perdió la cara al derbi y se puso 2-1 con el gol de Rüdiger en el 89'. Ante el Villarreal no marcó, pero defendió el 1-0 los más de 20 minutos que estuvo con 10 tras la expulsión de Vinicius. Y Roma, donde en ocho minutos remontó un 3-1 en contra para lograr una victoria tremendamente valiosa en lo deportivo y en lo anímico. Espí, uno de los grandes artífices de estos minutos de furia del Real Madrid, desveló la clave: "No queremos rendirnos, teníamos ganas de ganar el partido". Sea como fuere, el Madrid, zarandeado por el ruido deportivo y extradeportivo, está sacando los resultados adelante. El balance es de ocho victorias y dos derrotas en 10 partidos. En Liga, el comienzo arrollador del Barça, que la pasada temporada había cedido cinco puntos en las primeras ocho jornadas, deja a los de Mou en una situación incómoda, pero en Champions el Madrid está en el 'top 8' con pleno de puntos. Una circunstancia que ha querido reivindicar Bellingham, que deja un mensaje directo al pesimismo que rodea al equipo. "A veces hay partidos un poco más difíciles, pero casi todos los hemos ganado", apunta el inglés. Una afirmación que se sujeta sin miramos a la pasada temporada, en la que reinaba el optimismo a estas alturas. Mou resiste cualquier de los dos comienzos de Xabi Alonso. Si tomamos como referencia el Mundial de Clubes, el Madrid firmó ocho victorias, un empate y una derrota en los 10 primeros partidos con el ahora técnico del Chelsea. Si el punto de partida es la Liga, el Madrid arrancó la temporada con nueve victorias y un empate.

articles.title: Vitor Matos: Swansea boss on Jurgen Klopp influence and challenges of managing in the Championship
articles.summary: Swansea boss Vitor Matos spent five years as an elite development coach at Liverpool, but it would be unfair to paint him with a Jurgen Klopp-shaped brush entirely.
articles.body:
When Vitor Matos took charge of Swansea in November 2025, concerns around a potential relegation were on people's lips. Yet almost one year on, the Swans sit top of the Championship 10 games into the season.

In retrospect, the hire appears to have been a masterstroke considering the fact that Matos had only managed 12 senior games before moving to Swansea - those coming in the Portuguese second division.

Behind those 12 games, however, lives a coaching journey spanning 23 years across many continents and a variety of roles.

Prior to his spell in charge of Maritimo, the 38-year-old spent five years working under Jurgen Klopp as an elite development coach at Liverpool, before joining Red Bull Salzburg as Pep Lijnders' number two.

I called the Portuguese manager to explore his influences, principles and the ever-changing tactical landscape.

Building a squad on a foundation of counter-pressing feels apt for Matos when you consider the time he spent working under Klopp.

"Liverpool influenced me a lot in terms of counter-pressing, pressing, intensity, and what makes you grow as a team," he said.

"The most important thing is how much you believe in your idea and this style is how I see football. That's why I wanted this to be the foundation for our team."

Although the influence is clear, it would be unfair to paint Vitor with a Klopp-shaped brush entirely.

"I started at a really young age wanting to be a coach and was influenced by many different styles," he added.

Evidence of these many influences are clear to see in Swansea's game-model this season, with Vitor pulling together ideas from his time at FC Porto, Shandong Taishan and Liverpool.

Matos detailed his list of priorities when he replaced Alan Sheehan at Swansea.

"The most important thing was to make the team feel confident again, to make the players fall in love with playing with each other," he explained.

"For that, we wanted to take steps first on making the team much more aggressive without the ball.

"Giving them that boost of confidence by demanding a more aggressive game, creating a good feeling after a high regain or a wonderful tackle – it creates a better mood inside the group."

"Before I arrived there was also some change between a back four and a back five. I thought the squad was built for a back four at that time and to give consistency to the players, sticking with that was another priority.

"So, in our 4-3-3, we had a clear idea - to become a pressing and counter-pressing team, brave enough to take that risk.

"But then it's about, trying to find out the ways to be more aggressive."

In that sentence, Matos subtly revealed a key thread to his managerial approach and one that came up time and time again throughout our conversation.

He spoke about his many fixed footballing principles but believes the route to accomplishing those ideas must be shaped by the players at his disposal.

As a result, he takes a holistic approach to each player, seeking to understand them deeply, as footballers and human beings. Only then does he know how best they can work within his system.

"We want to press but where will we set up in terms of starting positions?" he continued.

"Who should start the press? Which are the triggers? Who are the players who buy in more or are more ready for this type of style in a short period of time?

"When you start from the players you have in front of you, you start from a position of comfort for them. This allows the players to be more confident which helps you to build your idea over time."

"When I spent time with the youth of FC Porto, I developed my understanding of positional play," Matos explained.

"We used a very positional 4-3-3, understanding the spaces, the timings, waiting for the ball to arrive to you at the right time. Players moved the ball until gaps started opening."

This season, we have seen those principles, honed at Porto, become the basis of an impressive Swansea side.

"How we solve problems depends on if we play against a man-marking team or a complete zonal team," said Matos.

"When you play against a complete zonal team, the most important thing is that you understand that you need to move them. By moving the opposition, you create spaces, you create a free player."

Much of the historic success of positional play has been underpinned by that same idea – finding the free player.

Against zonal defences, an attacker can occupy a gap between opponents and become a free, unmarked player. If a defender comes across to mark him, they risk leaving another attacker unmarked elsewhere.

But the rise in man-to-man pressure in recent years presents a different challenge. With defenders following individual opponents, the free player can cease to exist altogether.

To solve this problem, Matos has drawn on his time in China for answers.

"In China, I understood that to arrive at a more positional game, you could have different steps beforehand," he said.

"There is a benefit to having more players close to each other, rather than spreading them over space.

"If you spread them over space, you are demanding that, technically, they can solve many situations one-v-one. If they come closer to the ball, you can generate more possibilities. You can create a tempo that allows other players to be better in the big spaces."

It is unique style of play but these overloads have given Swansea extra solutions around the ball, helping disorganise both zonal and man-marking systems.

Matos added: "Especially if you play with a midfielder outside, you can overload one side a little bit more. Let's exchange the ball here five times, eight times and then when we go, we really go."

'With our two full-backs, we can tweak a lot of things'

Knowing that good positioning, overloads around the ball, and relentless off-the-ball running help Swansea disorganise defences, it is likely the dynamic and roaming full-backs that embody these qualities best.

Both full-backs have been used as tactical tools to undo a team's defensive strategy too:

"With our two full-backs, we can tweak a lot of things because these are normally positions where, especially if the opposition defend zonally, it's harder to press," Matos said, shedding light on why many top coaches have experimented in this position.

"Opponents need to make a decision on how they're going to press those spaces. And by pressing those spaces, there is the potential to create a lot of unbalance in the structure."

'Only when you are yourself can you really add value to something'

Successful young coaches are often praised for their tactical acumen, but management is as much about the moments away from the tactics board.

Matos, only 38, feels like a bridge between coaching generations.

"In the end, what I try to do is to value everyone in the right way. I try to make the best of everyone and try to allow everyone to be themselves. Only when you are yourself can you really add value to something," he said.

"The time with Jurgen was massive regarding that. How he was as a leader, how he took care of the club, how he took care of the players - that moulded a lot of me."

Now Matos draws on that experience for his own player-focused approach.

"I come from Portugal, but someone will come from Argentina, Brazil, Germany or the UK. And all of us have different ways to arrive at this specific moment," he said.

"Maybe I had a good house to live in and maybe one of them didn't, so he might be more emotional than me. Trying to understand them, trying to have sensitivity to that, is important.

"Knowing all of that, in the end we all are here for one thing: to win the next game."

articles.title: 😵‍💫 Homebody syndrome hits: Can this star only shine in the Bundesliga?
articles.summary: For three years, Christopher Nkunku had been searching for his old self. At Chelsea? He had terrible luck with injuries. At Milan? He did a solid job, but no...
articles.body:
For three years, Christopher Nkunku had been searching for his old self. At Chelsea? He had terrible luck with injuries. At Milan? He did a solid job, but nothing more. Only now, back in Leipzig, is the Frenchman really turning on the style again.

Last weekend, he even scored a hat-trick in the 6–0 rout of a helpless Frankfurt side—a "perfect" one by Germany's strict definition: three consecutive goals in a single half. It was the first in the Red Bulls' ten-year Bundesliga history.

So is Nkunku a classic case of someone who can only do his business at home? It's not quite that simple. But there are good reasons why the attacking star has rediscovered his explosive form in Saxony, of all places.

Finally fit instead of constantly injured

When Chelsea splashed out around €60 million on Nkunku in the summer of 2023, expectations were enormous. After all, the technically gifted forward arrived in England as the newly crowned Bundesliga top scorer and Player of the Season. But injuries repeatedly set him back.

The 28-year-old never really found a consistent rhythm at Milan last season either. In Leipzig, they know his injury history. But they also know exactly how good Nkunku can be when his body cooperates. There's a reason he racked up an impressive 70 goals and 56 assists in 172 competitive appearances across all competitions during his first spell at RB. That talent obviously hasn't simply vanished. Rather, Nkunku first had to lay the groundwork to be able to deliver consistently again.

Probably the most important factor in that respect was his decision not to spend the three-week international break putting his feet up. Lacking fitness after being demoted in Milan, he worked with a personal trainer in Leipzig and then trained at RB too. "I knew I had to work on my physical problems, and that's what I tried to do during the international break," he explained, drawing a clear conclusion: "I think that was a good decision."

But an attacking focal point like Nkunku needs more than just the legs for the job—he also needs a role that suits him. Under Martín Demichelis, the 18-cap international plays behind centre-forward Rômulo, where he can put his strengths to good use. He moves between the lines, links up with teammates and bursts into the box at just the right moment.

Little wonder Demichelis raves: "He shows what a talented player he is in everything he does." Captain David Raum also stresses: "When he gets going, he's a massive asset for us." Sounds like an environment that knows exactly what it has in its returning star.

The natural result is an impressive report card so far, with six goal involvements in just seven matches. It really is quite simple: Leipzig gives Nkunku trust and the right tactical setup, and knows exactly how to make the most of his strengths. Whether that really makes him someone who can only do his business at home is for everyone to decide for themselves. Sometimes you simply have to return to a place where you once felt comfortable. A little nod to Niclas Füllkrug here.

articles.title: Five losses: Michael Carrick must finally put an end to haunting Daniel Farke statistic vs Leeds
articles.summary: Michael Carrick will be looking to get one over on Daniel Farke for the first time as a manager tomorrow.Manchester United make the trip to Yorkshire to lock...
articles.body:
Michael Carrick will be looking to get one over on Daniel Farke for the first time as a manager tomorrow.

Manchester United make the trip to Yorkshire to lock horns with arch-rivals Leeds United in a 2pm kick-off.

In the meantime, Opta has shared a hugely concerning statistic that the Old Trafford faithful will be hoping comes to an end at Elland Road.

Since taking the leap into managerial roles, Carrick has lost all five league games in which he's come up against Farke.

Farke has dealt the United boss his most defeats, so the unwanted feat will undoubtedly be at the back of Carrick's mind when he takes to the dugout on Sunday.

5 – Michael Carrick has lost all five of his managerial league meetings with Daniel Farke, suffering his most defeats as a manager to the current Leeds United boss.Showdown. pic.twitter.com/o6FF7svrKM

It's safe to say that a win is also imperative for the former Red, with his tenure already being tipped for a premature end due to United's dismal start to the campaign.

What has Farke had to say about under-pressure Carrick?

Across their opening nine matches in all competitions, United have been on winning side only twice, against newly-promoted Ipswich Town in the Premier League on August 30 and against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah in their Champions League opener on September 10.

They have drawn against Everton, Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur, while losing to Hull City, Manchester City and, on Tuesday, Atletico Madrid.

Remarkably, Falke actually took the time to rally behind Carrick in his pre-game press conference on Friday, saying: "We don't have many young British coaches in the Premier League. We have a promising one, who has done excellent jobs at Middlesbrough and when [he] came in at Manchester United to steady the ship.

"But after six games, when they haven't had a horrendous start — okay, by their perception [they have], as they want to challenge for the title. The criticism has started already. I don't like it. If we have young promising managers, let's look after them, especially when you look at what he's done for the club over many years as a player and a coach in a very difficult situation. He did a tremendous job.

"We should back young British managers. Yes, I have a German passport, but I'm not too far away from getting British status. I like it when young British managers come through. The outside world wants to see everyone fail. We should be happy to have someone with so much potential and not question them too early."

articles.title: A major challenge looms on the horizon for Manchester City and Enzo Maresca
articles.summary: Manchester City have made a strong start to the 2026-27 season. Prior to their 4-2 loss to PSG, Enzo Maresca’s side had won eight consecutive matches in all...
articles.body:
Manchester City have made a strong start to the 2026-27 season. Prior to their 4-2 loss to PSG , Enzo Maresca's side had won eight consecutive matches in all competitions. It is clear to see that this new-look City side is beginning to click and grow together. However, due to the heavy fixture list and the importance of every match in the Premier League and UEFA Champions League, it is difficult for Enzo Maresca to provide his key players with the rest that they need. But rest for Manchester City's most important players is required at times so it is a major problem that Enzo Maresca had acknowledged.

Enzo Maresca knows that he will have to rest key players throughout the season.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledged that Erling Haaland will need to be rested at some point in the near future. Haaland has carried a heavy workload for both club and country this season. Also, Haaland had a busy summer with Norway at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, like many of his teammates. Maresca added it wasn't just Haaland who will need to be rested on occasions this season. He explained, when talking to the media yesterday , ahead of Manchester City's upcoming Premier League fixture against Ipswich Town: " At some point we probably need to give him rest, some days off. "

" We are thinking about this not just with Erling because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams. "

" Elliot, Enzo, Marc, Erling, Rúben – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest ."

Manchester City do have depth in their squad which will be needed.

Juggling the fitness and fatigue of key players is an issue that Enzo Maresca will have to confront throughout his first season as Manchester City's manager. Off the back of a busy summer for a host of City's players, a close eye will have to be kept on the players' fatigue levels. There is no doubt that this will occur and is already in progress now. It will be an ongoing process throughout this season. What Manchester City will not want is to lose key players such as Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez, Marc Guehi, Ruben Dias and others for extended periods.

To avoid this, Enzo Maresca will have to rotate his squad throughout the season. Fortunately, City do have the necessary squad depth to do this. Enzo Maresca will have to utilise his entire squad throughout the season. There isn't an ideal period for Maresca to rest key players. Manchester City's fixture list is relentless and there are no easy games. Instead, Maresca will have to trust his squad and continue to use clever substitutions as he has already this season. That will be a juggling act for Maresca, but it is one he is capable of putting together.

Enzo Maresca is fully aware that he will have to rest key players such as Erling Haaland throughout the season. That cannot be avoided. Luckily, he has a strong squad to call upon and hopefully this will be what helps Maresca give the rest to key players that is needed while continuing to push for results.

articles.title: Bundesliga centurion Atubolu applauds Frankfurt fans and Koch after first home win
articles.summary: Noah Atubolu kept his first clean sheet in Eintracht Frankfurt colors as the Eagles finally ended their winless home run on Friday with a 1-0 victory over Kö...
articles.body:
Noah Atubolu kept his first clean sheet in Eintracht Frankfurt colors as the Eagles finally ended their winless home run on Friday with a 1-0 victory over Köln. The ex-Freiburg shot-stopper conceded 16 goals in his first five games, including a 2-2 draw with his former club.

"I'm very relieved and happy that we won. It felt really good," Atubolu said after his 100th Bundesliga appearance. "The first home win of the season. And, for me, the first home win in an Eintracht jersey. Köln had a great chance early on, but overall we were very solid."

Marius Bülter came close to score within the first minute, but the visitors failed to keep that up for the rest of the game. Despite his costly mistakes in some of their defeats, including last week's game in Leipzig, Atubolu played well in both of their victories. The 24-year-old saved his sixth consecutive penalty-kick when Frankfurt won 3-1 in Mainz on matchday 3.

"We defended well together. Everything doesn't always have to be perfect in football. Not everything went smoothly, but if we play so compactly and maturely, we can get a lot of points. We have a lot of quality in attack and we know we're always good for goals. But the focus also has to be on defense, and Robin Koch deserves special mention there. He had a tough week, but played an incredible game. He's a leader, he led from the front and cleared everything away."

Frankfurt's coach Adi Hütter also praised his captain for his performance after a difficult week for both him and the club. In addition, Atubolu applauded Frankfurt fans for standing with the players and coach after the game in Leipzig.

"In Leipzig, the fans had every reason to be angry with us, but they applauded after the game. At that moment I thought to myself: 'Wow, what a club!' And it continued today. They pushed us for the full 90 minutes. The fans were one of the reasons why we were able to pull off this gritty victory."

Frankfurt will face Borussia Dortmund in Topspiel action on matchday 7. They will then clash HSV in two competitions, including their cup tie at Volksparkstadion on October 27th.

articles.title: Oklahoma football news: Brent Venables’ contract buyout details after 2-year extension, revealed
articles.summary: Oklahoma football made a significant financial commitment to Brent Venables, and the cost of firing him has already doubled. The Sooners. signed Venables to...
articles.body:
Oklahoma football made a significant financial commitment to Brent Venables , and the cost of firing him has already doubled. The Sooners. signed Venables to a six-year contract extension in August, keeping him under contract through January 2032.

The new agreement is worth $63 million, averaging $10.5 million annually. However, its buyout provisions reveal how expensive a coaching change could become.

According to George Stoia of On3, Oklahoma would owe Venables approximately $51.67 million if it fired him after the 2026 season. Without the extension, that figure would have been approximately $26.2 million.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The buyout decreases to $41.67 million after 2027 and $31.67 million after 2028. It falls to $21.67 million after 2029 and approximately $5.83 million after 2030.

Venables will earn $10 million in 2026, with annual raises of $200,000. His salary reaches $11 million in 2031.

The contract also includes performance incentives tied to postseason success. Venables can earn $500,000 for reaching the College Football Playoff, plus additional bonuses for advancing.

The financial details emerge during an uneven season for Oklahoma. The Sooners entered October with questions surrounding their offense and Venables' long-term future.

However, Oklahoma recently defeated No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry , securing a 27-24 victory.

That result provided a timely boost for Venables following earlier struggles.

Oklahoma's substantial buyout now adds another consideration to any future coaching decision. The extension offers stability, but moving in another direction would carry a high financial cost.

For Oklahoma, the extension represents more than a vote of confidence in Venables. It also raises the financial stakes surrounding the program's future.

Sustained success in the SEC could justify that investment, while continued struggles would make any potential coaching change considerably more expensive.

articles.title: Barcelona could revive pursuit of 20-year-old Premier League forward in 2027 after two rejected bids
articles.summary: Barcelona could return to the pursuit of Eli Junior Kroupi in the summer of 2027 after identifying the Bournemouth striker as a potential long-term option fo...
articles.body:
Barcelona could return to the pursuit of Eli Junior Kroupi in the summer of 2027 after identifying the Bournemouth striker as a potential long-term option for their attack, claims a report from SPORT .

The Catalan club considered the Frenchman last summer as an alternative to Julian Alvarez, but Bournemouth's valuation and the forward's injury complicated their plans.

Kroupi, 20, is now moving closer to a return after suffering a metatarsal fracture in July.

He has resumed on-pitch training following several months of rehabilitation, giving him an opportunity to rebuild his fitness and regain the form that attracted Barcelona's attention.

A future move remains uncertain, however, and Barcelona's interest will depend on their attacking needs and Kroupi's performances after returning from injury.

Barcelona transfer plans: Why Eli Junior Kroupi attracted interest

Barcelona's sporting management considered Kroupi while exploring options to strengthen the number nine position last summer.

Barcelona could revive their interest in Eli Junior Kroupi. (Photo by Eddie Keogh/Getty Images)

Alvarez was the priority target, but Atletico Madrid's reluctance made pursuing the Argentine an entirely different challenge.

Kroupi emerged as an alternative after an impressive first Premier League season, and his performances convinced the English club that he was a valuable part of their attacking project.

Barcelona submitted two offers for the French striker, but Bournemouth rejected both proposals.

The Cherries valued Kroupi at more than €100 million and were unwilling to sell one of their principal attacking threats, making an agreement difficult to reach.

Kroupi closes in on return after serious injury

Kroupi's injury in July interrupted his progress and complicated Barcelona's assessment of their attacking options.

However, the forward has now resumed training on the pitch as he approaches the next stage of his recovery.

Barcelona had two bids rejected for Eli Junior Kroupi. (Photo by Eddie Keogh/Getty Images)

His return will be important not only for Bournemouth but also for any club considering a future move.

Regaining match fitness and demonstrating that he can reproduce his previous performances will be essential if Barcelona are to renew their interest.

Could Barcelona revisit Kroupi in summer 2027?

On that note, Barcelona could reconsider Kroupi in 2027, although there is no guarantee that he will become a priority target.

This is because much will depend on the club's requirements at centre-forward and how their current attacking options perform over the coming months.

Hansi Flick has several players contributing to Barcelona's forward line, including Lamine Yamal, Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus, Raphinha, Dani Olmo and Fermin Lopez.

Hence, their performances and future transfer plans could influence whether the club needs to invest in another striker.

articles.title: "Lo bueno de remontar; lo malo de remontar"
articles.standfirst: 'Comprimidos', por Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.summary: 'Comprimidos', por Juan Ignacio Gallardo
articles.body: EEstos episodios asombrosos, increíbles, milagrosos, casi sobrenaturales que acumula el Real Madrid en competición europea; remontadas imposibles que el club blanco amontona de forma ordinaria, maquinal, como se apila ropa para lavar, esas noches mágicas tan frecuentes que hacen levitar al madridismo esconden un poderoso mensaje de tesón, confianza, convencimiento y orgullo. Lo que ocurrió el miércoles en Roma (ir perdiendo 3-1 en el minuto 82 y acabar ganando 3-4), seamos honestos, sólo lo puede hacer el Madrid. Nadie más. La lectura positiva de esta nueva remontada es constatar el espíritu indestructible de esa camiseta y el talento avasallador de esos jugadores. La lectura negativa de esa remontada es que, de nuevo, el equipo haya tenido que emplearse a fondo para, en pocos minutos, arreglar una desconexión futbolística que empieza a ser también demasiado frecuente. § La aparición de Endrick, fino, estilizado, veloz, desbordante, fue una de las grandes noticias en el Coliseo romano. § Uno de los grandes valores de Mourinho es cómo se pone de 'escudo humano' delante de sus jugadores, protegiéndoles. Esta semana logró desactivar de forma eficiente el run-run que sonaba en el Bernabéu en torno a Mbappé. § Hemos leído esta semana el informe que un ojeador del Barça envió al club tras ver jugar a Messi de niño. Era el año 2000, Leo estaba a punto de cumplir 13 años y el 'iluminado' (al que se le queda pequeño lo de 'tierra trágame') escribió: "CREC QUE NO S'HA DE FITXAR". Así, textual, en catalán y en mayúsculas. Esto me hace pensar en la finísima línea, en los minúsculos detalles que condicionan la vida. Si el jefe de scouting le hubiera hecho caso la historia, no sólo de Leo, también del Barça, de Argentina, del fútbol mundial hubiera sido, con total seguridad, completamente distinta. Ahora es una anécdota. Pero si llega a haber pasado... § En la gala Imperia (qué magnífico homenaje al universo deportivo femenino) escuché una frase colosal a Cristina Mitre (que reproduzco no de forma textual): "Lo importante no es cruzar la línea de meta, hay que aplaudir el hecho de llegar a ponerse en el arco de salida". § Raúl González, que ahora derrama talento jugando al golf, hizo el otro día en La Finca su primer hoyo en uno. § Me encantó ver a Nadal recogiendo el premio 7 Estrellas de la Comunidad de Madrid por su labor al frente de la Universidad que lleva su nombre. Campeón de todo, Rafa. Jódar, también premiado, no pudo asistir: estaba escribiendo la historia en Shanghai...

articles.title: England's 41-match unbeaten run ended by Canada
articles.summary: England's 41-match unbeaten streak ends in dramatic fashion as Shoshanah Seumanutafa's late try hands Canada a thrilling 24-21 victory in Toronto.
articles.body:
Tries: Bauder, Corrigan, Menin, Seumanutafa Cons: De Goede (2)

Tries: Feaunati, Harrison, Bern Cons: Harrison (3)

England's 41-match unbeaten streak ended in dramatic fashion as Shoshanah Seumanutafa's late try handed Canada a thrilling 24-21 victory in Toronto.

Canada, who previously snapped England's 39-match winning run with a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September, are the first team to defeat the Red Roses since November 2022, when they lost to New Zealand in the World Cup final.

Playing in front of 18,621 fans, a record for a standalone women's fixture in North America, the result also marks England's first defeat by Canada since 2016 and their first against their hosts on Canadian soil, having won their previous 11 away matches.

Canada's Savannah Bauder took advantage of Zoe Harrison's yellow card to open the scoring in the 15th minute, but it was England who took a 14-5 half-time lead, hitting back late in the first half through Maddie Feaunati and Harrison, with Laetitia Royer in the sin-bin for the hosts.

Sarah Bern cancelled out a stylish solo try from the hosts' Alysha Corrigan early in the second half to preserve England's nine-point lead before Canada's DaLeaka Menin crashed over for a converted score just after the hour mark to set up a tense finale.

Three minutes from time, Canada mounted an attack from halfway after a fumble put Harrison's clearing kick under pressure, and replacement Seumanutafa charged down the left wing to complete the comeback.

"We're not driven by outcome. We're disappointed by the result but there was some very good things in our performance. So we'll stick to our processes," said England head coach John Mitchell, following his first defeat since being appointed in late 2023.

"I guess [the loss] frees us up and allows us to find more. I know this group has got more in them. Sometimes it requires the context that we've just received to dig deeper and find something more."

The two sides will renew their rivalry in Ottawa on Friday, 23 October (in the early hours of Saturday on UK time) before England conclude their 2026 WXV Global Series against the USA in New Jersey on Friday, 30 October (21:15 GMT).

'We're still world champions, we're still number one'

This result has been coming for England, who showcased vulnerability in their three WXV Global Series home matches in September.

Against Australia, the world champions trailed at half-time for the first time since 2020 before roaring back with seven second-half tries for a 48-15 win. The following week, Canada held them to a draw in Exeter while a nail-biting 26-19 win over New Zealand at Twickenham was secured with the clock in the red.

This time, Canada's defensive resilience in the face of repeated attacks kept the world champions off the scoreboard until the 32nd minute, but England also lacked a clinical touch in their opponents' 22, with multiple opportunities going begging. Notably, Claudia Moloney-MacDonald had an early try chalked off for a knock-on in the grounding.

In defence, multiple penalties afforded Canada the freedom to form free-flowing attacks while it was an individual handling error when delivering the ball to fly-half Harrison which gave the hosts field position to score their match-winning try.

The result places England in uncharted territory, with several players in the squad never having tasted defeat on the international stage - winger Jess Breach was unbeaten in her previous 59 caps.

But for captain Meg Jones, it is no time to panic. England are "still world champions" and her message is simple: "Stick together, look out for each other, and we go again."

She added: "We've got to remember, there's a target on our back continuously. Everyone's got that underdog mentality, that underdog fight.

"We've got to be in a position now where we've got to be the quickest to respond. That's the nature of the game.

"What an amazing achievement for us as a group. I think they will go down in history as one of the best sporting teams.

"We're still world champions, we're still number one, and we'll still keep pushing to be the best we possibly can."

In September, Canada captain Sophie de Goede confessed she still has sleepless nights about her side's World Cup final defeat by England in 2025.

Even after ending the Red Roses' winning run in Exeter, she was frustrated at being denied the opportunity to go for the win, although reluctantly conceding that head coach Kevin Rouet's call to kick the ball dead was the sensible one.

After a historic performance in Toronto, where De Goede's side showcased "the DNA of our team" and "found a way to win", sleep might once again be hard to come by – albeit for far happier reasons.

"It's a little bit more than just the score at the end because we won on so many levels," added scrum-half Justine Pelletier. "Off the field, the crowd, being home. That win at the end on the pitch was just the cherry on [top].

"It was good to beat England but I think for a few years now, we knew that we could beat them. It was just a matter of time and a matter of putting every detail together."

England: Kildunne; Breach, Jones, Heard, Moloney-MacDonald; Harrison, L Packer; Botterman, Cokayne, Bern, Talling, Ives Campion, Burton, Matthews, Feaunati.

Replacements: Field, Carson, Muir, Short, Kabeya, Hunt, Rowland, Sing.

Canada: Bauder; Corrigan, Symonds, Perry, Hogan-Rochester; Tessier, Apps; Nelson, Idowu, Menin, de Goede, Royer, Smith, Omokhuale, Gibson.

Replacements: Tuttosi, Kassil, Rempel, Forteza, Buisa, Senft, Pelletier, Seumanutafa.
